issues.legal_issue: The claim that the deceased were the aggressors and that the accused acted defensively fails when the evidence establishes that the deceased side possessed the land and the accused went there to take it forcibly.
material_facts: The landowner’s daughter was found to be in possession of the land through tenants, including a deceased person who was cultivating it.

A revenue authority noted that one of the accused had stated he voluntarily relinquished possession, and a civil court had declared the daughter to be the owner in possession and restrained the accused from interfering.
The deceased and others were working in the field when the accused arrived armed and attacked them.
issues.conclusion: The deceased side was in possession of the land, and the argument that they were aggressors who prompted a defensive response was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the evidence of possession, including the revenue proceedings and the civil court decree, and found no basis for the claimed account of aggression. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this determination.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_convictions: The matter is a criminal appeal challenging convictions arising from an incident involving the disputed land.
predicates.opposing_side_possessed_disputed_land: The side later attacked was in possession of the disputed land, directly or through cultivators.
predicates.accused_arrived_armed_to_take_land_forci: The accused arrived armed with the purpose of forcibly taking possession of the land.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns an attack on land possessed by the opposing side and the accused arrived armed to take it forcibly, the claim that the opposing side was the aggressor is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A material and unexplained omission in an eyewitness’s prior police statement about an accused’s participation can make it unsafe to uphold that accused’s conviction on the witness’s evidence.
material_facts: An eyewitness testified to the participation of several accused in inflicting injuries.
In his statement to the police, the eyewitness had not attributed any injury to five of those accused, and he gave no satisfactory explanation when confronted with the omission.
The courts below had not considered this discrepancy, which the Supreme Court regarded as important.
issues.conclusion: The five accused were entitled to the benefit of doubt and were acquitted of the offences of which they had been convicted.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that an accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt when a material discrepancy undermines the safety of relying on the evidence against that accused. It considered the eyewitness’s statement recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. No earlier case was cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_convictions: The matter is a criminal appeal challenging convictions.
predicates.eyewitness_attributed_participation_at_t: An eyewitness attributed participation in the offence to the accused at trial.
predicates.prior_police_statement_omitted_that_part: The eyewitness’s prior police statement omitted the accused’s participation in the relevant acts.
predicates.no_satisfactory_explanation: The witness did not give a satisfactory explanation for the omission when confronted with it.

issues.definition: When an eyewitness implicates an accused at trial but omitted that participation from a prior police statement and cannot satisfactorily explain the omission, the accused receives the benefit of doubt in a criminal appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction may be based on common intention, or altered to reflect common intention, where the evidence establishes a prearranged joint attack and omission to frame the relevant charge caused no prejudice to the defence.
material_facts: Three accused went to the field armed with deadly weapons as part of a prearranged plan to attack those present and take the land forcibly.
They acted together in the attack, and each participated in acts that furthered the plan.

Although charges under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code had not been framed, the Supreme Court examined the charge sheets and evidence and found no prejudice to the defence; counsel conceded that there was no such prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The convictions of the three accused were sustained or altered to reflect liability for acts committed in furtherance of their common intention; the absence of a charge under Section 34 did not prevent that result because it caused no prejudice.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code to acts committed by several persons in furtherance of their common intention, distinguishing that basis of liability from liability under Section 149. It held that the omission to frame a Section 34 charge did not cause prejudice on the facts. No earlier case was cited.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_convictions and prearranged_joint_attack and each_accused_participated_in_furtherance and omitted_common_intention_charge_caused_no_prejudice

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_convictions: The matter is a criminal appeal challenging convictions arising from a joint attack.
predicates.prearranged_joint_attack: The accused acted under a plan made before the attack.
predicates.each_accused_participated_in_furtherance: Each accused participated in conduct that furthered the common plan.
predicates.omitted_common_intention_charge_caused_n: The relevant common-intention charge was not framed, but the omission did not prejudice the defence.

issues.definition: When accused jointly carry out a prearranged attack, each participates in furtherance of it, and omission of the common-intention charge causes no prejudice, their convictions may be sustained or altered to reflect common-intention liability.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence should not be distinguished from the lesser sentence imposed on co-participants in the same murder without a justification for treating the offender differently.
material_facts: One accused received a death sentence for a murder while co-participants in the relevant offences received imprisonment for life.
The court found no real justification for distinguishing that accused’s case from those of the co-participants for sentencing purposes.
issues.conclusion: The death sentence for that murder was altered to imprisonment for life.
issues.legal_principle: The court required a justification for differentiating the sentence of one participant from that of co-participants in the same murder. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_death_sentence: The matter is a criminal appeal against a death sentence for murder.
predicates.co_participants_received_lesser_sentence: Co-participants in the same murder received a sentence less severe than the death sentence.
predicates.no_justification_for_differential_senten: The court finds no justification for sentencing the offender more severely than the co-participants.

issues.definition: When a death sentence is appealed, co-participants in the same murder received lesser sentences, and no justification for the difference is shown, the death sentence is reduced to a lesser sentence.
